title: Fixing AI Cross-Cutting Concerns with the Gateway Pattern
snippet: Cross-cutting concerns are software aspects that affect the entire application and are common application-level functionalities that span several layers and tiers. Examples include logging, authentication, and error handling.

title: Spring Boot: Interceptor. Primary purpose: to intercept the…
snippet: An Interceptor in Spring Boot is a component that intercepts every HTTP request before it reaches your controller and after your controller responds. Interceptors are part of Spring MVC and are managed by the DispatcherServlet, implementing the HandlerInterceptor interface from org.springframework.web.servlet.

title: Formal Policy Enforcement for Real-World Agentic Systems
snippet: Policy-relevant events in agentic systems span multiple agents, models, services, and tools, making policy enforcement cross-cutting rather than local to any single component. A holistic approach combines formal methods and Aspect-Oriented Programming to support both the formal specification and the enforcement of safety properties through runtime monitoring.

title: Stop Using Webhooks for CRD Validation | CEL Makes Kubernetes Admission Faster, Simpler, and Safer
snippet: By moving validation logic into declarative policy objects that run natively in the API server, you eliminate the operational overhead of webhook servers while maintaining powerful validation capabilities. For many use cases, CEL admission policies can completely replace custom webhooks, reducing complexity and improving reliability.

title: Interceptor pattern
snippet: The structure of intercept design pattern is such that it has a filter, filter chain, filter manager, target, and client. Interceptors form a chain that always surrounds and invokes a fixed target operation, ensuring every interceptor executes both before and after the target regardless of outcomes.

title: Balancing Cross-Cutting Concerns in Clean Architecture
snippet: Cross-cutting concerns belong in a layer where they can be expressed once and enforced consistently. Authorization is a cross-cutting concern where enforcement must be interposed at every action and consult policy-relevant context accumulated across the execution.
